entries.name: Event-stream order-book reconstruction and best-three snapshot writer
entries.category: offline preprocessing solution; not a trading strategy
rules: Filter raw daily records to the requested Series.
Build bid and ask books by BidOrAsk, maintain orders by OrderBookPosition and OrderNumber, and add or reduce QuantityDifference according to its sign.
Aggregate live orders by Price, remove zero net-quantity price levels, sort bids descending and asks ascending, then write up to best_price_number levels; checked-in call sets best_price_number=3.
Output uses a TimeStamp marker row followed by Bid,Bid_Quantity,Ask,Ask_Quantity rows; price values are later divided by 100 in downstream notebooks.
The checked-in main update loop is range(index_find + 1,100), so this source is a limited prototype rather than a complete production reconstruction run.
entries.data_requirements: Raw order events with at least Series, TimeStamp, BidOrAsk, Price, OrderNumber, QuantityDifference, OrderBookPosition, BestPrice, and BestQuantity. Data rights are unknown/unlicensed.
entries.deployment_status: offline static transformation only; no streaming source, service, order routing, or paper-execution interface

entries.name: Three-level snapshot decoder, quantity cleanup, and market clock normalization
rules: Read transformed snapshot blocks where timestamp is taken from Bid_Quantity[0::4] and levels 1 through 3 are read from rows 1::4, 2::4, and 3::4.
Divide bid and ask prices by 100; replace NaN quantities at all three bid and ask levels with zero.
Parse timestamp character positions into seconds and express the intraday clock as seconds since 09:00 (subtract 32400).
entries.data_requirements: The repository-specific four-row-per-snapshot best-three CSV layout, timestamp strings at the expected character positions, and best-three bid/ask prices and quantities. Rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: offline notebook helper; no general schema adapter or real-time feed

entries.name: 600-second forward-cross binary label
entries.category: offline research label; not an executable entry/exit strategy
rules: At each represented one-second time i, select the latest order-book event at or before i.

For i before 25200 minus traded_time, label 1 when current best bid is greater than the minimum best ask from the selected event through the latest event at or before i+traded_time; otherwise label 0.
The checked-in dataset build calls traded_time=600 seconds.
For the last traded_time seconds, the code compares current bid with the final ask instead of a full future window.
entries.data_requirements: Timestamped best bid and best ask level-1 series across the session. The label needs future observations and is therefore offline-only by construction.
entries.deployment_status: label generation only; no order instruction or live label availability

entries.name: 900-second forward-cross label prototype
entries.category: offline research label prototype; not used by the checked-in model-selection dataset builder
rules: At each second, label 1 if current best bid exceeds the minimum best ask through a 900-second future window; else label 0.
The notebook also has a microsecond/event-time variant with the same 900-second look-ahead and an active 13:00-to-16:00-minus-900-seconds example.
This differs materially from the later builder's 600-second horizon.
entries.data_requirements: Timestamped level-1 bid/ask values and at least 900 seconds of future data; rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: feature-exploration notebook only

entries.name: UP/DOWN session dataset split
entries.category: offline dataset construction; names are time-session partitions, not directional strategies
rules: Feature_DataFrame_UP builds seconds 0 to 8999, annotated 09:00 to 11:30.
Feature_DataFrame_DOWN builds seconds 14400 to 25199, annotated 13:00 to 16:00.
Both call the same forward-cross label function and use the same 64 input features; they are not long versus short rule sets.
CSV writer emits separate _UP and _DOWN files; Model_Selection loads both but assigns data_2014=data_2014_up.
entries.data_requirements: A full session with the coded 09:00-based time convention and all rise/depth features. Rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: offline partitioning only

entries.name: One-second feature sampling with carry-forward on no update
rules: For a second containing one or more events, take the last event in that second and append its thirty rise and thirty-four depth values.
For a second with no event, append the previously appended label/feature values (carry-forward).
At the start of each configured session, calculate an index anchor at time 0 or 14400 for feature indexing.
entries.data_requirements: Event-timestamped level-1 through level-3 book series plus the feature arrays defined in this repository. Rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: offline research alignment; no event-time live feature engine

entries.name: Ask1 rolling rise-ratio feature family (30 lookbacks)
rules: Replace zero Ask1 values with the mean Ask1 value.

For each tick, calculate 100 times (Ask1[t]-Ask1[start])/Ask1[start], rounded to five decimals; before the lookback is available, start is the first observation, otherwise it is the first observation at or after t-lookback.
The model dataset computes 30 Ask1 features at lookbacks 6:00, 6:30, 7:00, ... , 20:30 minutes.
These thirty values are the first thirty non-label columns of the builder's feature vector.
entries.data_requirements: Timestamped best ask (level 1) and session-relative seconds. Rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: offline feature calculation; no live feature service

entries.name: Ask1 and Bid1 10-minute rise-ratio exploration
entries.category: exploratory feature analysis; not a model-input or trade-rule implementation
rules: Apply the same percentage-change construction separately to Ask1 and Bid1 using a fixed 600-second window and first-observation fallback.
The notebook evaluates selected January 2014 dates (16,17,20,21,22,24,27,28,29) and concatenates their rise values into histograms.
Chart-only horizontal reference levels are -0.4, -0.15, 0.15, and 0.4; no coded condition maps them to an order or position.
entries.data_requirements: Three-level snapshots for the selected dates and an external local raw-file layout hard-coded by the notebook. Rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: context/reference: feature calculations are present but no complete trading rule is stated

entries.name: Weighted three-level depth ratio and imbalance feature family
rules: For weights (w1,w2,w3), define Weight_Ask=w1*A1+w2*A2+w3*A3 and Weight_Bid=w1*B1+w2*B2+w3*B3.
Emit both W_AB=Weight_Ask/Weight_Bid and W_A_B=(Weight_Ask-Weight_Bid)/(Weight_Ask+Weight_Bid).
The active builder uses 17 weight triplets: 100,010,001,910,820,730,640,550,721,532,111,190,280,370,460,127,235 (digits denote relative weights as coded).
Thus the builder contributes 34 depth values to each feature vector.
entries.data_requirements: Simultaneous best-three bid and ask quantities. No zero-division handling is specified in this method. Rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: offline feature calculation; no real-time normalization or safeguards

entries.name: 50/30/20 market-depth, Bid/Ask ratio, and spread distribution analysis
entries.category: exploratory feature analysis; not an implemented strategy
rules: Sample each best-three quantity once per second by carrying the latest snapshot at or before that second.
Compute Bid_weighted=0.50*Bid1Qty+0.30*Bid2Qty+0.20*Bid3Qty and the symmetric Ask_weighted quantity.
Compute Bid_weighted/Ask_weighted and chart reference values 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, and 1.3; compute a plotted best-level spread as Ask1/5-Bid1/5.
No entry, exit, sizing, or mapping from these reference levels to an action is coded.
entries.data_requirements: Three-level snapshots for the notebook's selected dates. Rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: context/reference only; no complete decision rules

entries.name: 15-minute future min-ask / max-bid exploratory series
entries.category: offline look-ahead analysis; not deployable signal logic
rules: For the 1/16 exploration, calculate the future minimum Ask1 and maximum Bid1 over a 900-second horizon where available, then plot them beside current Ask1 and Bid1.
The notebook also computes all-remaining-session min Ask1 and max Bid1 series for charts.
Because these series explicitly use future observations and no action mapping is coded, they are labels/visual analysis rather than a deployable strategy.
entries.data_requirements: Complete future order-book paths for each evaluated timestamp; rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: context/reference only; look-ahead offline analysis

entries.name: Rolling CV-selected binary classifier research pipeline
entries.category: offline research strategy; no deployable execution implementation
rules: Use column 0 as binary label and all remaining columns as model inputs; the builder supplies 30 rise plus 34 depth features, i.e. 64 inputs.

For each window, take latest_sec=1800 rows as training data and the following pred_sec=10 rows as test data; choose hyperparameters for each candidate using five-fold GridSearchCV scored by accuracy, then fit and predict the test block.
The P&L cell chooses the candidate with the highest contemporaneous five-fold CV accuracy and uses the final prediction in its ten-row test block as submission.
The checked-in pipeline loop is range(0,10,pred_sec), so with pred_sec=10 the active example evaluates one window; a longer full-day loop is only commented out.
Although both session CSVs are loaded, the active assignment is data_2014=data_2014_up.
entries.data_requirements: Repository-specific labelled UP CSV with column 0 plus 64 feature columns, requiring prior top-three book reconstruction. Rights unknown.
entries.deployment_status: offline notebook research only; no model serialization, live market data, order submission, position state, risk controls, or Expo/native paper app

entries.name: Best-CV-model P&L evaluator
rules: For each prediction window, select the candidate with the largest stored CV accuracy and take its final predicted class and final true class.
If predicted class equals true class and is 1, append profit=0.2*column 65 at selected 10-second offsets; class 0 appends zero.
If predicted class is 1 but true class differs, append loss=0.2*(column 67 at current offset minus column 67 600 seconds later); predicted class 0 appends zero.
Plot individual tick P&L and cumulative sum.
entries.data_requirements: A model output plus CSV columns 65 and 67 at stated offsets. The checked-in feature builder only constructs label plus 64 features (columns 0 through 64), so the required price columns are not generated by the shown builder.
